posts.name: jffdougan
posts.cooked:
OK, in a couple parts:

- First, after preorder shipping has completed and GtG has finished moving into their new office, are there plans to do a warehouse party to celebrate the release of WCos?

- If the answer to the above is yes, I would like to propose that, as part of the event, a delegation take a selection of games - including but not limited to SotM - and pay a visit to the children's ward at Barnes (Memorial Hospital). My thoughts are inspired in part by the discussion that happened here: http://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/182555/item/3596458#item3596458

I know that St Louis has a pretty well-known children's hospital, and right before I moved to North Carolina the local gaming group had done an event at the local Ronald McDonald house to help brighten up the day of some of its residents. It seems like it would be a good thing to do.

(mods, please move this to an appropriate forum if deemed appropriate)

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
My lack of response was due to a lack of being on the right continent, but I like the idea.

I don't know how things work over the pond, but the thing that would concern me about it would be checking all the necessary child protection boxes - over here you can't just walk into a hospital or school with a bunch of people and some games and interact with children.

I needed a Criminal Records Bureau (CRB) check (which can take weeks to process) and had to attend child protection training and fill in a lengthy form to sing carols for a couple of hours with children in a hospital with parents, hospital staff, other members of my choir, and my choral director and his wife who are both teachers. Same for teaching children opera and African music.

This stuff's just not obvious to anyone who hasn't done official volunteering, so I thought I'd point out in case - apologies if you already know about it or this isn't relevant for the US!
